I have a broader view of the issue.

The problem really isn't religion in and of itself. The problem is people who believe that whatever it is that they believe is rightly imposed on other people - people who refuse to tolerate the simple fact that other people believe other things AND who have no respect for the right of those other people to believe those other things.

That is, underneath it all, the exact problem with religion, but religion is just a vehicle for that. It's not the actual cause, as demonstrated by the millions of people who simply hold their beliefs and never bother others with them. The real problem is the people who refuse to respect the individual sovereignty of others - who simply presume that whatever it is that they believe should be forced on other people and that the desires of those other people count for absolutely nothing. And yes - religion is a particularly common thing around which those people rally, but it's far from the only thing. They use any number of different vehicles for that - from social justice to patriotism to vegetarianism to... atheism.

It doesn't really "enrage" me that people do that. I don't know if that's a cause or an effect - if I have the luxury of a broader view of the issue because I'm not subject to that sort of emotion or I'm not subject to that sort of emotion because I have a broader view of the issue, but in any event, it just doesn't stir that sort of (arguably destructive) passion in me. It frustrates me, and irritates me, and saddens me, and that pretty much regardless of the specific vehicle one or another person might use for it. I count the overarching attitude - the lack of respect for the individual sovereignty of others and the parallel belief that ones views are rightly imposed on them - as the actual problem, and the specific nature of those views as ultimately trivial.
